A skeleton was slowly walking down the center aisle of the old stone temple.

If Jadis had to rate the kinds of monsters she found most threatening or terrifying, skeletons would have to be near the bottom of the list, maybe beating out bedsheet ghosts by a slim margin. What exactly was supposed to be scary about a skeleton? It was just a collection of bones, a natural part of any person’s anatomy. Nothing about any depiction of undead skeletons had ever seemed like anything other than a joke to Jadis.

The shambling mass of mismatched bones that slowly stalked down the dimly lit aisle towards her was nothing like the playfully spooky images Jadis had seen in cartoons and movies.

Dozens upon dozens of bones were stitched together in an asymmetrical jumble. It had three heads, clustered in a triangle at the top of a stubby bone torso, each of them from some different animal clearly unlike the others. One large arm ending in a club-like limb swung from the creature’s left side, four smaller arms with human-like hands sprouted from the right. It had two legs, each with more knees than a human leg could accommodate. A tail swung behind the abomination, balancing it as it leaned forwards, moving with the slow and deliberate steps of a hunter that had spotted prey.

Jadis hesitated for a few heartbeats as the bizarre amalgamation of bones took a few more clicking steps towards her. Stunned by the appearance of an actual undead monster walking before her, she voiced the first unthinking reaction that crossed her mind.

“You aren’t one of D’s priests, are you?”

The bone beast vibrated its disparate skulls together in a startling clatter before charging towards the dais.

Jadis stopped hesitating. Working solely on instinct, Jadis shot her arms forward and sent the wooden lectern flying at the monster, the crumbling piece of furniture slamming against the skeleton in a loud crash. She didn’t stop to see the result, however.

Before the bookstand had even struck bone, she was already running to the side. Without pause, Jadis dove through one of the broken windows and tumbled to the ground outside.

“Fuck that, I’m out of here,” she panted under her breath as she rose to her feet and began sprinting away from the temple and out of the skeleton-infested dead village.

Jadis had agreed to D’s pitch of living a life of adventure in a fantasy land, which did imply fighting monsters was going to be a thing. She was on board with monster slaying. One hundred percent interested in fighting epic battles against undead, demons, dragons, goblins, or anything else that could be reasonably expected. Hell, she’d be down to fight a dire rat or two, no problem.

But not when she was fucking naked.

Jadis ran full tilt into the darkening pine forest for a solid five minutes before slowing enough to take a look over her shoulder, certain the shambling travesty unto anatomy couldn’t possibly have followed her so far so fast.

The skeletal creature was a few dozen feet behind her, sprinting on arms and legs in eerie silence.

“Shit!”

Jadis redoubled her efforts into running away, no longer certain which direction she was even going anymore as the forest shadows grew longer and the light dimmer. She had to get away from the monster, put some distance between her and it and then hide.

Maybe she could climb a tree? Or maybe even find a cave to huddle in until the sun rose again and then she could get the hell away from the haunted dwarf village whose resident welcoming committee was trying to eat her skin.

Still sprinting, Jadis risked a glance behind and saw movement between the trees. The abomination was still chasing. The ache in her legs and lungs was telling her she couldn’t outrun the persistent monster forever. Since it was made of bone, would it ever tire? Would it chase her endlessly, or at least until she was an exhausted mess lying on the ground, unable to flee any longer?

Jadis had to turn and fight.

Before she attempted to defend herself, though, she needed to select a class. She hadn’t chosen, hoping to learn more about her options from someone with knowledge of what she was getting into. Now, with a bloodthirsty skeleton snapping at her heels, she didn’t have the luxury to wait. Jadis was certain having a class, any class at all, was better than having none.

Gasping out a prayer to her patron god, Jadis focused on her menu and mentally accepted the only class that looked remotely capable of combat.

“D, you better not have fucked me on this one.”

Primary Class Selected:

Mirror Knight

The transparent gray menu briefly flashed before Jadis’ eyes before a sudden flare of white light blinded her, sending her crashing to the ground in a tangle of limbs.

“Ow! God fucking damnit!” She shouted, voice echoing in her ears as she struggled to regain her feet, eyes watering from the flash and the fall.

Just as her vision was starting to clear and she was halfway on her feet, a sharp, bony mass collided with her side, sending her right back to the ground. The monstrosity had caught up with her.

Straddling her prone form, the undead assailant grappled its many smaller right arms with hers, grasping and squeezing, doing its best to hold her in place as it reared its left club arm back to bring the heavy end down on her head. Scrabbling with the abomination, Jadis barely managed to get her right arm free in time to catch the deadly arm before it slammed down on her skull. She struggled, twisting and turning, trying to pull away as far too many arms tangled with hers, sharp bones tearing at her skin and wrapping around her throat.

And yet, Jadis wasn’t doing any of that.

Still, the fact that Tiernan did have a spell to give himself and two of his fellow companions the ability to fly was impressive. Jadis hoped Aila would soon be able to do the same.

While Sorcha repeatedly used her wand to cast invigorating blasts of witchy magic on all of those who were present, Amarantha’s cauldron began spewing out a green and blue cloud of sparkling gas. Despite the wind, the cloud didn’t blow away or dissipate but instead sought out everyone nearby and flowed inside bodies in a weirdly ghostlike fashion. Jadis could feel the difference the moment the aerated potion slipped through the gaps in her armor and sunk into her skin. She could feel both her Strength and Vitality become boosted, and her stamina felt even further charged, as though the reservoir of energy inside her had doubled.

She wasn’t the only one to feel invigorated, either.

“Ja! Endelig en kamp!” Halvor shouted as he leapt up onto the edge of the railing while brandishing his two axes. “Ha! I have been idle too long!”

“Wait, I haven’t finished casting the spell you dolt!” Tiernan shouted as the crazy barbarian leapt into the sky. “Shit!”

Halvor went a lot higher and farther than Jadis would have expected, even considering his supernatural Strength. She figured the leap had to be assisted by some kind of a skill. A second after the Berserker took to the sky, an ethereal green glow surrounded the man. In a flash, the magic shifted into a pair of nebulous wings that were the color of the sky on a stormy day. Shouting with apparent glee, the barbaric maniac soared on ahead, his flight aiming straight for the two approaching dragons.

“Fucking idiot,” Tiernan cursed as he moved his hands in another wizardly spell, this time aimed at Rein. “I’m going to just let him fall one of these days.”

Jadis had cast her own wings by that point, all three of her selves having exited the airship in all of the rush. Aila had followed Jay out onto the deck and the redhead had her staff in hand.

“I can hit the dragons if they come close, but our balloon is vulnerable to attack from the breath dragons can spew.”

“I’ll try to keep them away,” Jay told the mage. “But I can’t promise anything. We should have Sabina fly us closer to the ground, just in case we need to bail.”

“We’ll do that,” Aila nodded. “But maybe I should ride with you? One of you can carry me while I cast spells.”

“No, you should take me, instead,” Meli interjected as she came up behind the redhead. “If you can take me closer to them, I might be able to speak to dragons.”

“You can do that?” Jay asked, thinking back to the Dryads in Weigrun and the great ice dragon, Vetregin. “Will they listen to you?”

“Possibly,” Meli shrugged. “Dragons are magic beasts. I am a Dryad. They might listen to me.”

“Might.”

Meli shrugged again.

“I cannot control magic beasts. They may ignore me entirely.”

“Alright, well, it’s worth a shot,” Jay said and took Meli up in one arm. “Aila, if this turns bad, I’ll be back for you. Let’s hope these dragons are reasonable.”

As all three of Jadis took to the sky, their spectral tendril wings glowing in the fading light of dusk, she saw Wilhelm leap over the edge of the airship deck. Unlike Rein, who was right next to him, he did not have any magic wings. However, before he had fallen even a dozen feet, a large winged quadruped swooped by and the Hero landed on the beast’s back. Taube, the Hero’s griffon, had been following the airship the whole trip thus far, and Jadis was impressed to see how well the man and his pet bird-lion worked together.

“And away we go!” Tiernan shouted as a glowing platform of purple lightning shot him like a rocket past Jay. “Gods, I love flying!”

Altogether, including herself in the count, their aerial team consisted of Severina, Noct, Tacitus, Wilhelm, Tiernan, Halvor, and Rein. Ten people against two dragons didn’t seem like good odds, until one remembered that almost everyone involved were powerhouses that could be considered small armies unto themselves. Jadis hadn’t seen Tiernan, Halvor, or Rein fight before, but if they were anything like Wilhelm or Ludger, who she had fought beside in the past, she had every confidence in their abilities.

That said, since there was a possibility of not having to fight the duo of giant winged lizards that were on a crash course with the Leviathan, Jadis used all of her magic-powered flight speed to race ahead of the others. While her Dys and Syd selves shouted explanations to the rest, Jay carried Meli with great speed towards the two dragons. As they got close, she was finally able to get a good look at the beasts.

Jadis had seen two dragons in her life thus far, and by the fortune that fell over her life, she had fought both of them. The first had been Vetregin, a massive ice dragon whose wings had blotted out the sky above when he passed overhead. Jadis didn’t have a precise gauge for the ice dragon’s size, but he had made a blue whale seem stumpy by comparison. The second dragon had been the withered and possessed black dragon that had tried to kidnap Alex. That beast had been relatively small compared to Vetregin, but whales were still the only comparable animal when it came to size.

These two new dragons were somewhere between in size. Not quite as colossal as Vetregin, but definitely larger than the decayed Demon dragon had been. The first one, the one that they had originally seen circling the mountain peak, was the larger of the two. The dragon had bright red scales on its back and sides, but its underbelly was a brilliant mix of yellows, oranges, and blues. The vibrant shades went from the tip of the red dragon’s tail all the way to where its neck and head met. The red dragon’s wings also had a mix of swirls and spots on the membrane between its wing bones, and the patterns reminded Jadis of a moth. That comparison was reinforced when she saw that the top side of the wings were the same dark red color as the rest of the dragon’s back; it was only the undersides where the nearly obnoxious shades of color were present.

The second dragon, who was lagging behind the first, was slightly smaller and had a slenderer build than its red companion. Its scales were ice blue, nearly white, but there was a pattern of emerald green diamond-shaped patches that went all along its back and sides, with greater density in the middle than further out. The ice blue dragon’s tail was also exceptionally long and whiplike compared to the red’s, and its tail’s color slowly changed in a gradient from blue to green the closer it got to the tip.

The closer Jay and Meli got to the charging dragons, the more details she saw. The red dragon had many thick, short horns crowning its head, while the ice blue dragon had longer, thinner spikes that moved almost like a porcupine’s quills. The red dragon’s eyes burned a bright golden color, while the blue dragon’s eyes were blood red. The most important detail, however, was that both dragons looked healthy and uncorrupted. If either were demonically possessed, Jadis couldn’t tell by her naked eye.

At that thought, Jadis recalled that she did not have to rely on her naked eye alone. Quickly casting Eyes of the Succubus on herself, she scanned the approaching Dragons for any sign of demonic magic. The spell didn’t reveal Demons specifically, but Jadis had been practicing, and she was getting decently good at telling the differences between types of magic. She felt that if there was a second source inside one or both of the dragons, she would be able to tell.

The magic auras of the two dragons flowed around them like great, multicolored storm clouds. For both beasts, the magic followed the color schemes of their scales surprisingly closely, though the magic itself was far more fluid. There was no sign of any separate or distinct extra magic within the aura of the red dragon, so Jadis presumed that the beast was Demon free. When she scanned the second dragon, though, she spotted an irregularity.

In the belly of the ice blue dragon, Jadis spotted an aura that was different from the rest. It was a mix of reds, greens, and golds, all swirling together in a tight bundle. While the colors were decidedly distinct from the greater aura of the blue dragon, the shape and overall feeling of the smaller bundle was the same. Jadis likened it to seeing a storm cloud within a storm cloud, as odd a thought as that was, since they were so similar.

“Shit, I don’t think that’s a Demon,” Jay said as a suspicion struck her.

“What do you mean?” Meli called out over the wind. “I don’t understand your words.”

“Meli, can you tell if that blue dragon is female?” Jay shouted her question, well aware that they were mere seconds away from making contact with the two gigantic beasts.

“I cannot be certain,” the Dryad shouted back. “I need to see the vent at the base of the tail.”

“Okay, well, get ready to check,” Jay adjusted her hold on Meli and her war hammer. “Because I think that blue dragon might be pregnant.”

If Meli made any response, Jadis didn’t hear it, because at that moment the red dragon opened its toothy jaws and let out an ear-splitting roar. The very metal of Jadis’ helmets rang with the howling noise, all other sound struck from existence as she was completely deafened. Clenching her teeth from the pain of just the dragon’s voice alone, Jay maneuvered so that her flight would bring her past the big red beast’s left flank. She wanted to get Meli closer to the smaller blue dragon so she could confirm her suspicion, if possible.

A moment before Jay would have dove past that huge red beast, she saw the dragon throw its wings wide, drastically slowing its forward momentum as the great membranous wings caught against the wind. In an instant, the dragon had gone from a sleek bullet to a massive kite in the sky, the whole of its yellow, orange, and blue underside on display. Since she had her Eyes of the Succubus activated, Jadis caught the millisecond that the dragon’s magic aura surged inward in response to the beast’s call for power.

“Watch ou—” Jadis didn’t even have the chance to finish her warning, much less move out of the way before the dragon’s magic struck.

A great flash of multi-colored light erupted from the scaly beast. It was like having a thousand strobe lights bursting in her eyes, and for a moment, Jadis thought she might have lost her vision entirely. She couldn’t even tell if her eyes were open or closed; all she could see was a swirl of burning colors.

Blinking her eyes as hard as she could to try and clear her vision, all three of Jadis pulled back in their flight, shooting straight up in an attempt to give her selves a second to recover from the debilitating magical attack. While Resilience helped her when spells struck her directly, it seemed that there wasn’t much it could do to lessen the effect of a stupefyingly bright light.

As she flew upwards, Jay felt a sudden hard pressure latch onto her lower legs. Blind and still partially deafened from the dragon’s roar, she instinctively curled up, protecting Meli with her armored arms. A second later, her body was jerked around like a ragdoll, before an even greater pressure pushed down on her whole body. Slamming her legs in what she thought was an upward direction, Jay pressed her feet into the crushing force while her back was stuck against something that was both hard and squishy at the same time.

As her eyes began to clear, Jay saw a confusing sight through the spots and colors still clouding her vision. Red and ivory surrounded her, with flashes of the ground and the sky caged on the edges of her sight. It wasn’t until the splatter of foul-smelling drool hit the front of her helmet that Jay put together what she was seeing with what had happened.

She was inside the maw of a dragon.

While I’m not saying Hraustrekr is right, his POV does have merit. Pre-Industrial revolution times, the world was a single pie governed by a zero sum economy. The economic value of the entire human race was a relatively set value, and the only way to get more was to get a piece of other people’s slice. Contrast to that, consecutively giving to others is also a surefire way to lose slivers of your pie. So, only on his reasoning for why they shouldn’t consecutively be the one who aids others, is exactly correct.

This is also part of why it took so long for humanity to get to the point of universal human rights. Providing such rights was just infeasible for their current economic powers, and the political system was also not conducive to such change. Democracy was able to be fully implemented mainly due to the widespread adaptation of long range communication and education; when people were able to understand what was happening around them, as well as communicate about their experiences and ideas across the territory, that was when “letting your voice be heard” became a thing. From nation-wide postal services and newspapers to telegrams and radio and even television broadcasts, democracy steadily gained a platform to operate on, and as globalization and industrial production became mainstream, universal human rights became very much doable.

Today, we can do simple math to prove that our respective governments have near to more than enough money to fund most if not all programs that would benefit communities, whether it be from taxing the top 1% or from confiscating ill-gotten wealth of corrupt politicians. In whatever fantastical-medieval world Oros is in though, this is highly improbable. Even factoring in magic, it appears to be a rare and limited resource, and most importantly, one that cannot be shared nor used in mass production the same way as industrial machinery. Long range communication, if even possible, is likely safeguarded by the military for strict government use only. Unlike our current positive sum economy, where the more people who can participate in the economy, the better the economic turnout, in current Oros, helping others is a liability you need to prepare to spend on. So the prince isn’t wrong when he says blindly saving them like superheroes will only waste resources. It is true, even in our modern age. That’s why we don’t just blindly save people then leave them to their devices.

Unlike what Hraustrekr thinks is a good idea, the proper approach would be to sign cultural exchanges, trade agreements, and resource sharing pacts with neighboring nations. Truly, instead of conquering land, you conquer the economy and the culture; send experts, scholars, and missionaries to other nations in exchange for receiving some of theirs to train, expanding the influence of your services and culture whilst receiving influxes of fresh blood and ideas from different cultures in different regions. The temples in particular, I’m sure, would benefit the most from these. Unlike our religious organizations, these temple groups are loyal to their divine doctrine and are actually beholden to the god they swore to serve. They get free real estate (basically) as well as insights on other regional interpretations of holy scripture and whatnot.

While it would be a true fight for the long game (you’d be losing a lot initially. Like, a lot lot) it will speedrun them to a globalized (well, continent-wise) cultural and service economy in what, a couple of hundred years? I’m no economist and I have literally no basis for any historical context that could support that, but we got here with printing machines and the earliest steel mill iterations in only half a century, so giving it ten to twenty times that without any machinery but magic is fair game. Imperial leadership is mostly elves anyway, so long game for us isn’t very long for them.

Now, what we do know, about the impending failures of Hrastrekr’s wonderfully brilliant plan, is that his plan (or any authoritarian with wet dreams of world domination, really) works on, mainly, four assumptions:

* That any region annexed will accept being integrated.

* That the regions annexed successfully will remain loyal (and accept your culture).

* That the Imperial caste will be able to manage the region in place of the local government better and more successfully.

* That the Imperial caste sent to manage the annexed and likely far removed territories will stay loyal through the generations.

To explain in order, (1) is unlikely because no matter how heroic you are, how great your contributions are, unless the local lord was so unbelievably corrupt and incorrigibly evil, the people have a say in their cultural identity. They will not appreciate being taken over by anyone. Even if some don’t mind, perhaps out of gratitude or admiration (the Philippines is an example, during the time the US “liberated” them from Spanish imperial rule) eventually, they will likely decide to rule themselves anyway. This segues into (2) and (3), because any culture will always resist change brought about by foreign influences, regardless of if it’s the foreign culture acting on the local one or the local one acting on the foreign culture. While the both cultures will eventually mix, it takes time and immersion, and definitely not something that you want taking place in any seat of power. While Oros is mostly one continent, they still have their own sub-regions and, I’m sure, their own niches and quirks. If nothing else, the multiple races, languages, and environments will certainly have a tangible impact on the style of leadership necessary for the region. Someone who has ruled plains and fields for a long time, like Eir’s father (I’m sorry, I can’t recall his name), is unlikely to find much success in ruling a coastal region unless they rigorously research the area and its culture. Where he once defended against droughts and pests, he now has to deal with wind and storm surges, fresh seafood export, and grain import.

Nobles who spent their lives living in forested hills won’t be able to easily adapt to arid, snowy regions. Can you imagine Vraekae ruling the Noxian clans? (I actually can, help ). Now while I’m sure there’s some good overlap, the Empire can’t possibly afford to subsume the entirety of Oros under only its own resources. Any economic power in a zero-sum economy is physically incapable of it; just ask literally any power that tried to maintain their colonies in the last 300 years. By the tail end of it, the annexed territories were actually draining their expenses because it took so much to get them out of the post-war economy and into functioning money-makers.

Granted, there’s no world war here in Oros, but regions ravaged through Demonic infestations will likely suffer similar economic consequences as those struck by the world wars in our time. Even if one simply instated a sort of proxy leadership that only reported to you and you just kept on a leash, what good would it serve them? To the local government, the Empire would just be uselessly looking over their work even though they have very little to offer or advise. Their interference may even be detrimental, considering the lack of context they possess about that regions climate and operations. In the end, it’ll eventually end in either a provisional government that will eventually become its own separate entity, or civil war. Just look at the America’s own history of attempts at being “the world’s police”, which ended spectacularly in… civil war. Vietnam? Civil war. Afghanistan? Civil war. Philippines? Civil war. Captain America: Civil War.

The only benefit is that any problem can be supported by an assembly of Imperial experts, but that is essentially sending them to learn about the region and work with its people to formulate an innovative solution which involves… pretty much what the whole cultural exchange is about, but minus the political time bomb. And that’s not touching on (4), which is assuming that anyone you send there won’t just randomly decide they wanna do their own thing now and defect from the Empire. Literally. Literally a good portion of our historical kingdoms came about through this mechanism. Without intermittent communication between the edges and the capital, the trickle of services and goods will eventually die out before it reaches the outskirts. It’s the age-old Shortest Path Problem. The shortest path will eventually be so long that the outskirts will basically be doing their own thing to support themselves. For hard to reach areas, modern governments usually defer to decentralization, where they increase the power of local government units to hasten response time and remove their reliance on faraway resources stored in central governments. There at the outskirts, corruption will be at an all time high compared to the central ones. Much easier to get away with it when your entire circle is stuck at the edges, and reports to the central government is watered down through how-many-proxies as it is passed through multitudes of messengers on its way to the capital.

And remember that all of this is basically stemming from Hraustrekr’s salt with poorly skilled military from other regions. There are literally easier methods than going full tilt world domination. The main argument against giving out knowledge is that you don’t know if it’ll one day be pointed at you, and trade secrets are held tight by craftsmen. Still, for all the opportunities they have compared to medieval Earth, they should be much more capable of forming proper knowledge exchange programs, as opposed to going through the, ironically, logistical nightmare that is domain expansion. Really, no matter who you are, what time period you live in, or how much money you have, this kind of domination is infeasible. Hraustrekr may fancy himself a revolutionary who will save the lesser people beyond the Imperial borders, but other men than him have tried. Better men than him have tried. Men with bigger armies, bigger sticks, and bigger coffers have tried. They all failed. It is not a problem of skill or resources; it can’t be done. Only a species with a culture so homogenous could succeed at this (ants), and people are decidedly not homogenous. Hraustrekr is doomed to fail, just like every empire in history. The closest to success was probably Genghis Khan, and that was restricted to Central Asia, and he technically granted all of his annexed tribes religious and cultural freedom, which is basically the part where we talked about ruling technically but leaving them to their own hands basically

This is something I've been thinking about for a while, but thanks to this phrase, I now want to ask. How exactly does the distance between her bodies work? Because, to be honest, I see it this way:

Syd-----------------------3miles-----------------------Jay-----------------------3miles-----------------------Dys

Here, at least one, in this case Jay, acts as a central "core" from which the distance of the rest of the bodies is determined. So in this case, Syd and Dys can be, for example, 6 miles apart, but within the range of those 3 miles that Jadis feels she can reach, with Jay as the central point, which determines those 3 miles between their two bodies. And if we add the other two bodies, so now that she has 5, that distance can be multiplied even further, reaching up to 12 miles between one body and the other, at their furthest points, using Jay again as the central point, and Syd and Dys as a kind of relay.

-3miles-                                    -6miles-                                  -9miles-                                    -12miles-

Dia--------------------------------Syd-----------------------------------Jay-----------------------------------Dys-----------------------------------Ida

But there is the other option, in which each body must always be the same distance from the rest. That is, always in an equilateral triangle. There, none of them is a "core," but the distance is the same for all of them. And even if you increase the number of bodies, you'd just be adding another "triangle" (more like a straight line that can rotate there, but whatever) to the formula, turning it into basically a 5-pointed star. There would be a central point, but it would be an imaginary one. (In fact, now that I think about it, this is somehow very similar to the 3-body problem...)

So, which one is the real one? Because if the first one is correct, then the more bodies she have, the greater the relative distance they can separate, at least in a straight line.

It's that exact same writing style which is causing problems. There are two undeniable facts:

- Thea hadn't been able to keep up in fights with the best of the group - Jadis, Aila, Eir, and Kerr. She has been consistently relegated to second-line duty for hundreds of chapters. This makes sense.

- Thea left like ten levels on the table now.

I thought the solution to the first will be avoiding the second. We have no hard XP numbers or a level up bar; she might have been very close to 60 from the last fight, just didn't quite ding past 59. Imagine if she got her tertiary during the initial bird ambush on the airship. Between landing and starting the fight, she absolutely would have had time to pick it, then she could have gotten the largest gains out of anyone during the battle with a level one tertiary from the very start.

Now how will she catch up again? What scenario will allow her to gain levels that doesn't also give XP to anyone else on the team? Will we get a section where she leaves the company and goes grinding solo? How will it ever make sense that she can somehow stand next to Jadis again, when she is only ever falling behind on levels? How will that not break the worldbuilding?

Precisely because of the extremely admirable and impressive commitment to maintaining logic, consistency, and common sense, Thea suddenly regaining her position without justification will be a reduction in the quality of writing. Which leaves us with: she remains sidelined, the writing quality drops, or something insane happens to help her return. The last one is clearly the best, for me - but it could have happened here in Glanum. If that's the plan, we will have to wait until the next thing, and who knows when that will be; all the while Thea is just being carried.

My point isn't about disliking Thea at all. She is second place to Aila in my heart. I'm upset she is getting left behind. Thea has a very specific niche: she is their defensive fighter. I love her personality and contributions outside combat, but in the practical operation of the company, that's all she does.

I keep expecting her military training and experience to come up, but it never does - the Glanum battle would have been a prime opportunity for her to contribute to planning or properly liaise with the army, but neither happens. I kind of assume this aspect of her character has been quietly dropped - possibly because of harem size and word count limits and focusing on more important or fun things.

Kerr does scouting, speaks several languages, and is widely travelled. Aila is the brains of the operation. Eir is a priestess and a noble with all the knowledge those bring, and the mom of the group. Sabina is a genius. Alex - do I even need to say anything?

For Thea, there is now a lot of competition. None of these are defensive fighters in the same way, but they are all melee frontliners:

- Severina is level 100 and while we don't know her skills, her personality and approach in fights have tended towards defending people so far. She is clearly more capable of dealing damage than Thea, but her mindset seems closer to Thea than Jadis' "hit them first and hard enough that they never hit back". In both the capital and the Cold Brook ambushes, Sev fights quite defensively, prioritising the safety of others over a kill count.

- Alex is similarly more damage-capable than Thea, but she is very durable and has a nice set of defensive skills. With her XP bonus, she is blasting levels, and her classes are utterly insane. How much longer before she out levels Thea, and with three Jadis classes, completely makes her irrelevant?

- Bridget has no defense, but apparently the System heavily favours pragmatism over any kind of fairness, so her damage buff will keep boosting her levels sky-high even when she actually does nothing personally. She is the least direct competition for Thea's job, being a glass cannon, but is still a melee frontliner.

If Thea's role going forward will be to stand next to Eir at the back, and clean up the few Demons that are so weak and pathetic that double-size Jadis doesn't even spare the time to stomp on them, that sucks. That really sucks. That's the fighting equivalent of telling her "just stay home sweetie while the competent people handle the fighting".

Jadis is the protagonist, but scaling her to the point where her party members become irrelevant is unsatisfying as a story. To me, anyway. I know people love these insane power fantasies. But after the start where she was alone, being in a group and getting their help was a key part of her journey and an approach I really loved. It felt like a legitimate group effort, and it made this work stand out.

Jadis getting more and more HP and Fortitude while Thea not only doesn't keep up, but actively falls behind is depressing. It's like if Jadis unlocked a skill that makes her a better archer than Kerr, or a spell that costs literally one mana and outperforms anything Aila can do.

This has been an interesting discussion to read. I did not think that the line would cause so much confusion. I may have to rewrite some of the chapter to avoid future misunderstandings.

Avatar x Avatar has three possible outcomes. Avatar #1, Avatar #2, and a whole new hybrid species.

Avatar x Non-Avatar has only one outcome. A half-breed of the Avatar and Non-Avatar race that is Non-Avatar in nature.

Steingrimur and Rhyswynn are not avatars, but they come from avatar bloodlines and thus have "superficial" physical traits that set them apart from the rest of their kind and show their parentage.

If a Nephilim and a Demon were to have a child, for example, and the child born was a Nephilim rather than a Demon or a Succubi, the child would have some superficial traits showing its partly demonic origin, but for all intents and purposes it would be a Nephilim with primarily Nephilim characteristics.

Since I foresee this question, I'll preemptively ask and answer it: Why would the priests want Jadis to breed with non-avatars if the resultant offspring have no chance of being avatars?

The answer is: selective breeding. If you have a large enough population of half-breeds, you have the potential to breed the base species back into existence. It would take time and a large population to make it work, but it is possible. The mechanics of that plan were something that I had intended to discuss in the story many chapters ago, but it never fit right in any of the chapters and I ended up scrapping that scene. Maybe I'll find a spot for it in the future.

Let me state my own opinion on Agdistis and this story explicitly.

As for Agdistis, I think he is brilliant. Full stop. I love his writing, his approach, his narrative style and his character development.

I 100% believe Agdistis has what it takes to be a professional novelist. And I also believe he should be professionally published.

As for this story, I love it as well. I absolutely dig Jadis and would find it awesome to hang out with her if I could somehow be transported to Oros. Until such is possible, I will have to settle for following Jadis through this story.

As I said at the start, I wish I could have it a hardcover novel. At least for the arcs thus completed. I also think it's worthy of mainstream publication.

However, y'all had to know there was going to be a "but" given my first two posts... I do not believe that mainstream publishers would touch it.

Because I believe that my star rating should be used as a tool to help writers, I  cannot, in good conscience, give it 5 stars. That is because if I rate something with 5 stars, I am stating that I firmly believe that the author should make an honest effort to seek mainstream publication.

Now, it is true that Agdistis can break this down into story arcs and self-publish them. If that is Agdistis wants to do, then by all means. Plenty of far inferior writers self-publish all the time. In fact, posting to sites like this is just that. They are just publishing their work for free.

Just remember though, and this is why I think highest of mainstream publishers, they offer writers added value in the form of editorial staff and a marketing department to spread the word of the new novel to book sellers and librarians. An author who self-publishes has to either hire their own editor, find a volunteer (which we all gladly do) or do it themself. They also have to market their work on their own. And finally, if they want to do a physical copy to sell, they have to pay a publisher out of pocket to print and bind the books.

Shad Brooks, of Shadiversity, went that route with his first novel.

I do caution self-publishing via amazon. They are pretty monopolistic and, from what I have seen from other authors on here, like JamminRabbit, they force the author to remove large segments of their work from websites like here. They also bind them, legally, to not sell through other retailers like Google Play Books. That said, I think that is if a writer wants to offer their story through the kindle unlimited.

Personally, I despise amazon so what I know is second hand at best.

I am delighted to read all the votes of confidence.

If I were in Jadis' shoes, my approach to all of this would be to be as direct as possible with everyone, openly, and make sure everyone knows it. No subterfuge. Such direct boldness is, in its own way, just as effective a means at political intrigue as the various cloak and dagger methods. It uses the light of open, public honesty as a counter to the shadows of others.

The downside to this approach is that it requires the user to maintain absolutely zero privacy. At least not while it is being established that your honesty is as good as gold and can be banked upon. Once that is established, you can then begin to make your private life... well, private again.

The other way to handle things like this is to have agents, benefactors, and friends of your own who are skilled in cloak and dagger politics to act as a shield for you. But, the sort of shield that isn't there to keep it away from you so much as to be both your hands in the arena of politics and handle your public relations.

A great comparison for the type of person Jadis is and the situation she is in to another work of fiction is Honor Harrington. Like Jadis, Honor is a very direct, bold and blunt person. Like Jadis, she is prone to lashing out physically to those who would harm her and those she cares about. Like Jadis, she hates politics and did her best to avoid it, ultimately to her detriment. Like Jadis, she had friends and mentors who tried to help her out with it in her early career. And like Jadis, she ultimately had to engage in politics as her prominence in society and her accomplishments in battle continued to catapult her star upwards.

@Agdistis If you haven't read the Honor Harrington novels by David Weber, you might want to check them out. Jadis' story is remarkably similar so to the early career of Honor Harrington.

Honor's response to once she was no longer able to avoid politics was to be herself, blunt, honest, impeccable integrity, and above all else, true to herself openly before all.

It both made her, at times, more vulnerable to slander attacks, but also made it easier for her, and her partisans, to deal with them as well. Her vulnerability came in the form that accusations of her actions somehow harming her friends could hurt her. Her defense came about because of her towering reputation for honesty and integrity.

That is probably Jadis' best response to the Brunholdts as well. Just be, in a public setting, openly honest to how she views Elodie's father and WHY she views him that way. It takes the legs out from under her if she is truly engaged in some kind of subterfuge, and if she isn't, at least not entirely, could give her information that makes her rethink everything she knows or has assumed about Jadis based on any correspondence from her father.

Might even get her, and maybe her mother too, to break ranks with General Egilhard and to scold him for being a dunce while also extending an olive branch to Jadis. @anonjohn20 I think SeriousBlueJewel's "no" was to your statement about there being no 'shortcuts'. Truth is, because this is a Fantasy System World with magic and LitRPG, shortcuts actually will exist. The skill Sabina has is a good example.

Yes, a good architect/engineer/artisan will use math when developing their ideas and plans, but those skills can also provide them shortcuts in the form of intuitive knowledge and gut instincts that help speed up the process.

A good example of such instincts in our real life is the work done by stone cutters. They do not calculate where a fault in the rock may be before they split it. Instead they look at the rock, study it, plan the shape they want to get from it and then careful tap stakes into the stone. Once the stakes are partially in, along the line of fracture they desire, they hammer them home, alternating strokes on different stakes, and the rock splits along the desired line. From there, the rock can be taken to whatever is being built where natural stone has been requested and fits nicely into place without the need for any mortar. This is a very ancient practice.

Another example is how a truly experienced blacksmith can judge the quality of metal and its readiness to be worked simply by the color of the flames and the glow of the metal.

Now, are these substitutes for good engineering and good engineering practices? In the grand scheme, no. In the short run, it depends. In the ideal scheme, you'd combine both, good engineering practices with the intuition gleaned from experience, or in the case of Oros, experience and skills.

So they will exercise care depending upon who they are dealing with. This also means the subordinates of anyone who isn't the Emperor has to walk carefully.

The chapter 307 Hero information here

The class of Hero was always a primary class. The individual who received it would have many variations to choose from, but the class itself would be a Hero class. No one but the ordained Hero of Oros had ever unlocked a Hero class, which was not unexpected considering its providence. The Hero class was considered to be a divine gift from the gods, one that the pantheon only granted to one lucky individual as a response to the resurgence of the demonic forces of Samleos led by the Demon Lord. Without having a Hero class, a person could never be considered The Hero.

The other gift that every Hero received was a divinely mandated mission. Over the millennia that the demonic invasion cycle had repeated, every Hero born had always been visited by at least one god. This visitation often took the form of a dream, though it could be a more physical encounter depending on the situation. One of the gods who would visit the newly chosen Hero was always Valtar, while if there was a second, they would be one whom the individual most closely identified with in both their personal beliefs and past actions. Most Heroes of the past chose a class related to Valtar, but a strong minority had chosen classes related to one of the other eight gods. No matter which god the nascent Hero most identified with, the mission was always the same: Stop the Spawn of Samleos from destroying mortal kind and destroy the Demon Lord.

Along with the mission, the gods who visited the new Hero would provide them with a relic of some kind. Usually they were given a weapon, sometimes armor or a tool of some kind. This item would be imbued with divine power and was intended to empower the Hero in their progress towards becoming a force capable of defeating the demonic hordes invading the lands. The relic would also serve as an identifier, making it easy for the common man to know that this person was the Hero. Aside from some form of identification spell, this divine relic was the main way most people were able to identify who the Hero was at a glance. However, there were other hallmarks of a Hero that were relatively unknown beyond those of the priesthood and the upper echelons of the imperial government.

One of those notable qualities was the way the Hero affected the class options of their companions. It wasn't unheard of for one person to have an influence over another person's class. One of the most well-known examples were "Bonded" classes, though other examples existed like "Loyal Follower" or "Mortal Rival". Still, in the case of those influenced classes, the descriptor tended to have more to do with the feelings of the person who had gained the class than the person who stood as the focal point of the class. This was not the case for Hero-influenced classes.

The companions that a Hero could have with them always ended up gaining powerful classes that were more than just the standard variety of Bonded class. The impact that the Hero's presence had upon his closest adherents was pronounced and consistent. That was why every Hero had an Oracle to aid them, as well as Paladins, Arch-Wizards, and Bulwarks. To be the companion of a Hero was to accept the inevitability that both one's class choices and one's life were going to be altered. No one but the Hero had the ability to affect other people's classes with such power and regularity.

@GlassRose The nice thing about magic, gods and fantasy is that the author can just "hand wave" and solve all of their world building problems. In this case, we do not truly know if any of the languages on Oros have any  true resemblance to those spoken on here in the real world. All we know for certain is Jadis' perception of things.

A god can easily be granted the power, by the author, to give participants of their world the capacity to innately understand and comprehend a language just as surely as if they had lived that language their entire lives.

Take the anime, "Tsukimichi: Moonlit Fantasy", I do not know if you have watched it or not, but the main character is a young Japanese man, in high school, of very bland looks, taken from Earth and sent to a fantasy realm to be a Hero of the Goddess in charge of ruling and administrating over that world.

The Goddess in question, finding the young man's bland looks not to her liking, discards him and denies him the ability to understand and speak the common tongue of the "hyumans", that spelling is correct from the story, but he can speak, understand, read and write every other language in that world.

Now, he does go on to learn how to understand the common tongue, and how to read and write it, but labors under the belief he is cursed to not be able to speak it.

At the same time he still has his Japanese language that was raised in. The spelling of the fantasy languages is wildly different from the kanji characters of Japanese, so while he can easily think, as if a native, in the languages native to the fantasy world, he knows they are not Japanese.

Coming back to this story, we have not seen Jadis try and see if there is some kind of distinction between English and Imperial. All we have been given, so far, is that the symbols that represent letters and numbers are different, and that the native language Jadis monologues in her head is Imperial.

What we do not know is if Destarious transmuted her understanding of English into Imperial, or if Imperial is actually identical to English as spoke, but different when written.

Even if it should turn out that English and Imperial are the same as spoken, then Jadis can still teach them the letters and spelling of her own English as a cipher of the Imperial language that would let them communicate safely in private. It would also let Aila put her journal into a cipher only Fortune's Favored inner members would be able to read as well.

But, going back to how Jadis has come to understand Imperial, let us assume for the moment, for argument's sake, that English and Imperial are in fact different languages. We can then build upon that assumption, coupled with the fact that Jadis is able to understand and speak this language flawlessly, as if she were raised in it, to mean that as part of her reincarnation that she was given a natives innate understanding. Thus there wouldn't be any translating going on. She was granted the power of native understanding of Imperial as part of her new life.

This makes your entire example with a native English speaker, who also can speak and understand Greek, meaningless.

This is why this all goes back to Agdistis. What is the world building relationship between the languages of Oros to those of the real world? Until Agdistis tells us, either by story, here in the comments, or by world building companion guide, we truly do not know.

Until then, we can make guesses and offer suggestions to the author. Of course they author doesn't have to use them, but still, the making of them is what is fun. And, for now, all approaches and theories as to the languages of Oros, their relationship to the languages of Earth, and how they are perceived are all equally valid.

---Dealing with Those Who Annoy, Irritate, Bully, Harass---

Never said it was dumb for them to want him to be less of an ass and be more considerate of how his antics might be taken in advance. That said, Jack did think he thought they would have been more receptive given how his latest antic has given them a big boost and doesn't understand why they reacted as they did.

As to ignoring people who are trying to get under your skin, personally, I find it rather easy to do. Something I have had to learn to do out of necessity.

We tend to let what others say and think get to us when we care too much about strangers or people we do not like. Usually this is born out of a deep seated desire to be liked by others or of a deep, possibly suppressed attraction to the person who is antagonizing us. Regardless of why people care about what strangers and/or antagonistic/annoying others think, if we all cultivate a mindset to only care about the opinions and actions of those whom we care for, then it becomes much easier to ignore the words of those whom we do not care for.

I will grant, such cultivation does require practice. However, before that can be done, one must be aware the problem exists in the first place. This is why I suggest that they ignore Jack in the first place. This also has the benefit of teaching Jack that being an ass won't get it attention. So Jack just might learn to be a little more considerate in the future if its antics get less attention than it was hoping for.

One last thing, that I can't ignore, there does come a time when fire must be fought with fire. When retaliation against someone harassing you becomes the only appropriate response. Unfortunately, there is no clear set of guidelines to gauge as to when retaliation, punishment, or revenge becomes the right path in response to a bully/harasser. Each person must decide for themselves how much they are willing to tolerate and where the line exists. But, it is paramount that once that line is crossed, they stand up for themselves and push back. That they demand respect.

---On Avatars, Some Theorizing Included---

As to avatars, I never said they were a force of nature. I said the Fetch, and their antics, could be as akin to such.

A couple things are clear:

1) Avatars are reflections of the nature of their god or goddess, both in looks and in behavior

2) Avatars have free will, so they do have the agency to deviate from their patron's nature

3) Avatars can have dual aspects, possibly more -- this is seen in Jadis

Jadis tends to be lawful good most of the time. She can trend towards chaotic good when she is playing with/teasing her girls. Kerr is a lot like this too, but even more chaotic when it comes to teasing and ribbing others. But, both revert to lawful good when called for and genuinely care for others.

The rest of Fortune's Favored are all solidly lawful good.

This kinda fits in with what little we saw of Lyssandria and have heard of her. She is also the wife of the big, good god, who name I forget.

Destarious, on the other hand, son of Lyssandria, step son of the big, good god, is chaotic neutral through and through. He is very much an equal opportunity god of chaos, both good and bad. This is seen in what he represents, his divine quest to Jadis as a condition of her reincarnation, how people perceive him and his avatars, and how Jack has behaved.

Knowing what a god is, what they stand for, represent, and their nature is important in such worlds because they give people the necessary foreknowledge to be able to expect and anticipate how their avatars are most likely going to behave.

Not all avatars are going to behave as expected though. Alex the Demonling is a perfect example of that. Instead of following 'dear old dad Samleos' ' footsteps and being an agent of raw destruction, it has instead decided it would rather follow the influence of Jadis. Thus, in a way, it could be said it is following Destarious and Lyssandria instead now. This is an example of avatar taking maximum advantage of their agency over their own lives.

(Side note of which is that this also means Jadis could become a true avatar of Lyssandria only and not Lyssandria and Destarious together.)

If Jack does change, if Jack does eventually stop being an ass and becomes more considerate of others prior to pulling any shenanigans, that would also be an example of Jack utilizing greater agency to deviate from its base nature as Destarious had originally created.

One final bit, and this just occurred to me, much of what Jack said to Jadis about having free will and the influence of the gods being in the form of gut instincts and impulses, might have been a degree of partial fluff to soothe Jadis. Jadis isn't a natural avatar. Her soul doesn't even originate from Oros. It was also mature before it was reincarnated. Just food for thought. In the end, only Agdistis truly knows.

Arcane magic spells were elemental in nature, at least in the classical sense. Fire, water, wind, earth, and any of the various related subtypes like ice and lightning were all within the realm of spells an arcane powered class could cast. Powerful divine spells could heal injury, regenerate lost limbs, remove sickness and poisons, or even temporarily increase a person’s attributes. Eldritch spells were for making illusions or altering the physical form of the caster or target. Body and mind were the domains of eldritch magic. While no spells could directly alter or control a person's thoughts, false images and illusions could be cast upon a person, tricking or frightening them. The physical or attribute-based changes eldritch spells made to a person were also generally permanent or at least long lasting, unlike the temporary buffs divine magic applied.

If you want to use sand as a truly fearful hazard, then there are two ways to really go about it. The first is very powerful winds whipping up a sandstorm. This is the what we do, intentionally, when we build smaller enclosures for sand blasting metal. The sand then becomes an airborne sandpaper/file and very rapidly erodes exposed surfaces.

The other great danger for sand is that it is loose and not particularly compact. Thus, when adding additional factors like water or ground vibrations, sand becomes quicksand and things that step onto it rapidly begin to sink and become trapped.

This also makes building things on top of sand very very difficult. Like the ancient saw:

Make sure you build your house upon a foundation of granite, for a house built upon sand will surely collapse.

There are ways to build strong foundations upon sand though. They are called "friction foundations". They are composed of a large number of pilings placed into the sandy soil, going deep. Then across the top of all the concrete pilings you build your foundation for your structure. The weight of your structure is then born by the extreme friction generated between the pilings and the sand by the enormous surface area of all the pilings.

Mythbusters Phonebook Friction Myth: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hOt-D_ee-JE

Result: True

The sheer amount of friction from the interleaved pages of the two phonebooks was so strong that two 8 ton tanks pulling on them, with chains hooked up to think steel plates clamped and bolted to the spines of the books, that the spines of the books failed before the pages let go. The force measuring device reached several tons of pressure pulling on them before the spines failed.

Same principle, but in reverse to hold up large buildings built upon sand. This is how the foundation of the Burj Khalifa is made.

Foundation

The superstructure is supported by a large reinforced concrete mat, which is in turn supported by bored reinforced concrete piles. The design was based on extensive geotechnical and seismic studies. The mat is 3.7 metres thick and was constructed in four separate pours totaling 12,500 cubic meters of concrete. The 1.5-metre diameter x 43 meter long piles represent the largest and longest piles conventionally available in the region. A high density, low permeability concrete was used in the foundations, as well as a cathodic protection system under the mat, to minimize any detrimental effects from corrosive chemicals in local groundwater.

On the other hand, Skills always multiply each other so long as they can be applied to the same situation without doing the exact same thing, even if the multiplication doesn't happen in raw numbers and is only a small effect.

@BananaFaktory66 Technically, you would be correct. The key bit here is that this is a lit-rpg fantasy story. In an RPG a healer is usually considered a combat support, not a pure combat member. But, because healers keep the actual damage dealers and tanks alive and in the fight, they are usually treated as combat members  themselves.

This comparison doesn't hold up in reality though. Navy Corpsemen are embedded with the combat units they support. Their job isn't to keep soldiers and marines fighting on the front lines, but to keep they from dying when injured and evacuate them from the front lines to the rear. That is because we don't have anything like healing magic that can automatically mend wounds in seconds. If we could, then the comparison would hold up completely.

Going back to Eir, because she can mend wounds in seconds, restore hp, and keep the true fighters fighting, one can easily see her being considered a secondary combat member.

Sabina, on the other hand, doesn't have to be outside the city at all. She can get xp and level up just fine by crafting and mending armor and weapons for Fortune's Favored back in Far Felsen, safe and sound. The only reason she is actually with them is because Jadis wants to power level her and help her grow at a significantly faster pace. This boosts her stats and the skills she will have available to aid in her crafting at a much faster pace. This in turn will make practicing her trade much easier and faster to acquire the experience she needs to become a master, or grand master, artisan.

In short you can break down support roles by weather or not they remain useful if left behind in town verse only being useful if brought along. Eir is useless if left behind. She can't heal from Far Felsen. Sabina, however, can easily keep forging new weapons and armor for everyone while left behind.

There is another author on this site, and other sites, names Rakitan5. I had a very enlightening talk with her back on Hentai Foundry a few years back about the poly life as she is poly herself and been so for decades. A few insights she shared:

1) Communication is absolutely critical. Open, honest, earnest communication.

2) Rules, aka boundaries, are even more prevalent in a poly situation than with monogamy.

---People like to think poly would be less restrictive since the theoretical number of sexual partners available to everyone increases. But, that is actually wrong. Functional, sound poly relationships, with a solid foundation, have just as many rules, if not more rules, than relationships based on monogamy. The reason being that each additional person brings their own quirks to the fold. Each additional person also represents even greater risk to the fold as well. Without these greater rules, it becomes more easy, and more likely, that someone can be injured by another member, thus causing a rift in the community.

3) It is especially important that no one be neglected.

---That means which ever gender is in the minority must be sure to make sure they are available to spend quality time with everyone else. This not only helps prevent loneliness and depression, but also helps to ward of territorial feelings from arising and causing strife to form.

---Weather or not that means the direction of the group is decided by a single person, or collectively through democratic means, everyone must be on board with how things are handled. If the group is built around one particularly strong and dominant personality, then singular leadership might be the best way to go. If there are several, then as long as they can work together and develop a mutual vision, then democratic means might be the better way to go.

You can't hammer a wire out of a bar. You can heat a bar up though and push and/or draw it through a series of consecutive holes of ever smaller size. You can also take a bar of iron, heat it up, and push it through a roller mechanism that shapes the bar while applying force to make the metal conform to the shape. This is repeated until the bar has been stretched out and taken on a round form. You can find many examples of this on YouTube.

I did, briefly, spend some time working in a wire factory that produced copper and aluminium wire. They also coated the wire with insulated, produced armored cable for ultra heavy duty applications and even had their own on site copper foundry to for melting both recycled copper and raw copper ingots fresh from the mines into ultra pure copper for wire production.

In large scale wire production, the process of pulling a wire through progressively smaller holes is the preferred method.

When it comes to helical coils for springs though, much as shape matters, the composition of the metal also matters. Such metal also needs to be hardened and tempered as well.

@Agdistis

I think you made a mistake by wanting spring coils on that wagon. Yes, they do provide a higher level of ride comfort in passenger cars, but at the expense of far far greater complexity of suspension, far more maintenance, less load capacity compared to a similar strength leaf spring and more stress on the frame the spring is connected to.

That is why you will usually see leaf springs on heavy duty applications like commercial trucks and trains.

Also, coil springs are older than leaf springs. A fast look at the history of springs showed me that coil springs were in use in the Roman era and leaf springs weren't invented until the 1600s.

I suppose you could do leaf springs on the main suspension, then have smaller coil springs further isolating the passenger seats from the wagon body below. That would let the girls ride in relative comfort as Jadis pulls them while also keeping the main suspension both easier to make, cheaper and more robust for all the cargo to be carried as well.

When you read the line of her question, if you read it without commas, the entire context of the question changes. Closest how? In terms of physical location? Family location? @LordDarkfor I think the problem here is two fold. You are being too literal in how you are approaching what has been written within the chapter and also do not understand how creative writing works in practice.

Creative writing is meant to tell a tale. To do this, the author creates a vision within their own mind. This vision is the world, the setting, the characters, their hopes, dreams, desires, motivations, ambitions, relationships... etc. To convey all of this, they must write in such a way, that we the reader, are able to recreate this world in some fashion as we read their tale.

The best writers can do this in such a way to captivate their audience while leaving them free to use their imagination to flesh out the details, like just what sort of variation of the color blue a shirt might be, or the details of a face. Writers more new to writing will sometimes want to go into too much detail.

However, there comes a time when a writer must be precise because they wish to convey a very specific scene in a very specific way and leave little, or no room for creative interpretation by the audience. They do this because they have a goal within the story.

In this case, Jadis needs information and doesn't want to leave room for Destarious to wiggle out of it.

How does the author accomplish this? With very specific wording and punctuation. In past chapters, the author didn't pay attention to this and we, the community, started brain storming how different skills could be used. A moment to theorycraft what passives would be best for Jadis, right now, from her 4 lovers.

Aila is a no brainer. The passive that lets her drink Nephilim cum as a mana potion. Which has already been established as the most useful to Jadis.

From Kerr, we have a few options. In no particular order:

Bowman's Defense - Passive Skill. Increases the Vitality, Fortitude, and Resilience attributes by 3 points.

Ambush Tactics I - Passive Skill. Deal minor extra damage with any attack made against a target that does not detect you.

Practiced Polyglot - Passive Skill. Increases the ease with which you learn new languages.

Landmark Navigator - Passive Skill. Decreases the chances of becoming lost so long as you are within visible range of a known landmark.

Strong Stomach -  Passive Skill. Provides lesser protection from diseases and parasites that can be spread via ingestion.

Rest Anywhere, Sleep Everywhere  - Passive Skill. Your ability to rest and recover is boosted in locations and environments that would otherwise be detrimental to your health and stamina regeneration.

See the Hidden World - Passive Skill. You are more likely to find hidden paths or discover unknown locations when traveling in untamed wilderness terrains. Both objects and creatures that are hidden from you are more likely to be spotted. These benefits are lost in tamed, cultivated, or otherwise civilized environments.

Silent Dash - Passive Skill. Double the speed at which you can travel while still moving silently.

Just about any skill above has a good deal of versatility and usefulness. Some are exclusive to the battlefield, like Ambush Tactics I and Bowman's Defense, while the others are are straight up very solid skills for just all around adventuring and exploring. Some could even lend to establishing an advantage before starting a fight as well.

Seeing as Jadis is setting up to be the leader of her own merc outfit, aka adventuring company, Practiced Polyglot might be the most useful for dealing with a wider array of people down the road.

From Thea we have the following options:

The Long March - Passive Skill. Expend less stamina when on the move, allowing you to march greater distances before tiring. Weapons, armor, and other carried equipment cause less of a drain on stamina.

Improved Vision I - Passive skill. Provides a minor boost to your sight, allowing you to see over greater distances and spot details more easily.

Stable Footing - Passive Skill. You are more balanced in combat and less likely to trip or stumble when acted upon by an outside force.

It is a shorter list of unique skills here than with Kerr, but all 3 are even more powerful I think. With Jadis' new heavy armor, the first skill would go a long ways to ensuring it her already incredible stamina becomes even greater. Would also help greatly with pulling the group's wagon when they head out to do some demon farming.

Improved Vision is just.. the saying "knowledge is half the battle" is no joke. There is a reason having accurate information before you go into a fight can make all the difference and allow a much smaller force to annihilate a larger one. Being able to see farther and pick out details and other things would help bolster Jadis when planning an attack or defense.

Stable Footing, the name alone sells itself. The importance of keeping your feet and stability in a fight can't be overstated. It just can't. There is a reason every fighting style ever known and shall ever be known has always started with methods to keep your footing and keep stable.

About Vraekae.

I was checking information what Magistrate was. Apparently the role is based on ancient Rome. Consul and Praetor are alternatives to it.

Basically, it is a supreme commander over a region. Yet, there might be more than 1 per region. 2 was preferable, one leads army while another manages the city. Only regions engaged in war have such commanders. Peaceful regions are managed by the senate.

The role is most prestigeous but also very fickle. Few positions and many candidates. So if one underperforms, or even simply doesn't achieve any triumphs, they can easily be replaced. The positions have fixed service time and unless one has good support, then another will likely be chosen in replacement once the time is up. Or say if demons get completely eliminated from the region then a Magistrate will not be needed there.

In Vraekae case, it seems to me that she's new to the role, as she was given a region that was supposed to be relatively peaceful, with but a minor demonic incursion. If you do that though, also consider filing a formal copyright. By international treaty, you have a default copyright the very moment you started pressing keys on your keyboard. However, that default copyright is insufficient should you ever need to protect your IP in a court of law. International copyright treaties are some of the few treaties that are nearly universal, even with places like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. - This consistent effort to not take wealth offered is hugely inconsistent with all the other personality traits Jadis has demonstrated.

Jadis has demonstrated the following traits--this list is by no means all inclusive--selfishness, impatience, modestly narcissistic, arrogant, self-confident, brash recklessness, impulsiveness, high libido, lascivious behavior, sexual predator (hunter type, not be confused with rapist, she does, at least, respect consent), high sexual deviancy, authoritarian, alpha tendencies, intelligent, analytical, quick minded; just to name those that come to the top of my head.

One thing in common with most of these things is that these are all traits of someone who is not meek. People like this know what they want, and, depending upon morality, will do just about whatever it takes to get what they want. Not only do they desire the pleasures of the flesh, but they also seek material gain as well. For Jadis to constantly balking at taking payment for her actions, it is NOT in character with the materialistic side that her sexual boldness, domineering alpha traits all indicate. If she was behaving in character, she would accept payment for her efforts and take it as only her just due. Her narcissistic side would see it as what she is owed, her dominant side would see it as proper payment for actions, and her analytical and intelligent side would see it as more resources to fund getting her properly equipped to better tackle her newfound life of adventure. Both for her own sake as well as that of being able to better protect her first member of harem to be.

If you read, listen, and observe enough human interactions, you will begin to notice various personality archetypes. We call these archetypes 'stereotypes'. They exist because, as a good rule of thumb, they make an excellent base upon which a person can be characterized by. Thus, they also make an excellent base upon which to use when creating a character model.

One of the biggest flaws amateur writers in Japan have, is that they all too often do not write characters the properly fit a stereotype. This in turn influences a great many other writers outside of Japan thanks to the popularity and influence of anime, manga, and Japanese light novels.

I am making an assumption that this is a major source of both inspiration and influence for you.

I make this assumption both due to the predilection of such to be true with a great many authors on this website as well as the fact that it was Japanese authors that created and popularized the concept of the LitRPG sub-genre of fantasy and science fiction.

Now, as to how character created fail to fit a stereotype, what usually happens is they begin to use one, but they deviate from it too much. Their characters break the mold too often. Some breaking and deviation is necessary. Nobody ever truly fits a stereotype perfectly 100%. Sometimes they might tic all the major check boxes, but will also have traits, interests, hobbies, behaviors that partially match other stereotypes. Biggest mistake many writers make is insufficient use of the primary stereotype and/or usage of characteristics of stereotypes that are very much in direct contradiction to the base personality.

In real life situations and stories; those you might hear about, read, or even observe directly; people who are as sexually dominant as Jadis has shown herself to be, they also seek material gains in life too. Some will be big spenders, some will be quite frugal. All will seek to make coin, but how they handle that coin once made will be where the differences come in to play.

@Agdistis Something to consider when thinking of "hero". What is a "hero"?

Naturally, this is a philosophical question. Technically, there is no right or wrong answer. A "hero" will be whatever each individual defines one to be. But, if you are ok with it, I'd like to share my own definition of "hero".

A "hero" is someone who brings hope. A hero can bring hope in one of three ways. By action that inspires hope, by words that fight off despair and restore and/or kindle hope, or by simply showing up and thus showing everyone, yes, the dawn is coming.

Jadis has brought people hope with her actions in battle with demons. So she is a hero on the battlefield. She has brought hope to the clerics and politicians of the empire with her presence, the Nephilim have returned. The gods smile in favor once more upon all that is good and righteous in the world. She has brought hope through her words. She encouraged Aila that her dreams could still be achieved. And she was right. With her aid, Aila got her mage combat class so she desperately wanted.

Other stories are replete with similar examples. When Harry Potter arrives with Hagrid in the Leaky Cauldron and the old Witches and Wizards all react with awe and reverence, their hero has returned. When Captain America tells SHIELD that Hydra has infiltrated them and they can't launch those heli-carriers and the rank and file begin to refuse orders, citing "Captain's Orders". When the US general in "Man of Steel" lets Superman go and face General Zod. When Ironman sacrifices himself to undo the damage done by Thanos. Each of these is an example of one of  the 3 different ways a hero can bring hope to others. Some by words, some by action, some by simply showing up.

As to classical heros not taking payment for saving others, all of those examples were of people who already possessed all the resources they would ever need. As such, they aren't very good examples to rely upon. A better example.... hmm, to be honest, I'm having trouble thinking of a good example in popular mass media. Either way, yeah, pretty much all classical heroes we think of, like from comics and mass media, they all had pretty much everything they already needed. Either they were born with it or already had large organizations supporting them. Doesn't really fit Jadis' situation.
